title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Atka Mackerel in the Central Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
summary:
The National Marine Fisheries Service has temporarily closed targeted fishing for Atka mackerel in the Central Aleutian Islands for certain trawl vessels from October 31 through December 31, 2025. The agency took this step because that group’s 2025 total allowable catch is reached or about to be reached, and the closure helps keep harvests within legal limits.

Who benefits? This move is meant to protect the Atka mackerel population and keep the overall fishery on a sustainable path. Staying within the set catch limit supports long-term access to the resource, which can benefit fishermen, processors, and coastal communities over time. It also aligns with consumer expectations for responsibly managed seafood and with conservation goals that prioritize healthy ocean ecosystems.

Who might be negatively affected? Trawl vessels in this segment of the fleet, along with their crews and onshore processors, could see short-term financial impacts from losing two months of targeted fishing. Some coastal communities that depend on this fishing activity may feel the pinch through reduced landings and related business. Vessels can still keep small amounts of Atka mackerel caught incidentally while fishing for other species, within existing limits, but they cannot pursue it as a main target in the affected area.

The agency made the change quickly, without a prior comment period or a 30‑day delay, because new harvest data became available on October 28 and waiting could have led to exceeding the limit. While fast action can raise concerns about process, this type of immediate closure is a standard tool used to match management to real-time conditions and prevent overharvest.
